method: One EXPLAIN ANALYZE BUFFERS per case after count and result-ID checks. No forced planner settings, DDL, or statistics refresh. Temporary rows roll back. The marker condition is included in every case; these small-fixture observations are not a throughput or production latency benchmark.

advanced_all.sql: SELECT "tinkick_test_products"."id" FROM "tinkick_test_products" WHERE "tinkick_test_products"."description" = $1 AND (EXISTS ( WITH RECURSIVE tinkick_regexp_graph AS (SELECT $2::jsonb AS graph), tinkick_regexp_input AS ( SELECT ("tinkick_test_products"."name")::text AS value, char_length(("tinkick_test_products"."name")::text) AS length ), tinkick_regexp_run(position, state) AS ( SELECT 0, 0 FROM tinkick_regexp_input WHERE value IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT run.position + 1, (edge.value ->> 2)::integer FROM tinkick_regexp_run AS run CROSS JOIN tinkick_regexp_input AS input CROSS JOIN tinkick_regexp_graph AS specification CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(specification.graph -> 'edges' -> run.state) AS edge(value) WHERE run.position < input.length AND ascii(substring(input.value FROM run.position + 1 FOR 1)) BETWEEN (edge.value ->> 0)::integer AND (edge.value ->> 1)::integer ) SELECT 1 FROM tinkick_regexp_run AS run CROSS JOIN tinkick_regexp_input AS input CROSS JOIN tinkick_regexp_graph AS specification WHERE run.position = input.length AND specification.graph -> 'accept' -> run.state = 'true'::jsonb ))

ordinary_native.sql: SELECT "tinkick_test_products"."id" FROM "tinkick_test_products" WHERE "tinkick_test_products"."description" = $1 AND (name ==> $2) AND (("tinkick_test_products"."name")::text COLLATE "C" ~ $3)
